_note: Constants from index.html (the frozen design reference). Build-stat formulas and shop rules live in game/run.gd.

shop._reroll: starts at 1 + ceil(0.8*wave); each reroll adds ceil(wave/2)

economy._kill_scrap_falloff: scrap per cop kill x 1/(1 + falloff*(wave-1)); wave 10 pays 27%, wave 20 pays 15% per kill
economy._drop_chance: Brotato-style loot roll: a downed cop drops scrap with this chance (bosses always drop; civilians' cash and crates are separate). Modules add/subtract via the dropPct stat (clamped 5-100%). Each drop is worth 1/drop_chance, so income at the base chance matches the always-drop economy.
economy._note: 1.0 = the prototype's economy (every kill drop and cash pile pays in full). The heist campaign used 0.15 because heists paid big lump sums.

parts._note: Shop offers that swap the MAIN gun's ammo or frame. t = shop tier (same weights as items), c = base price (wave-scaled like items). A slot becomes a part offer with probability `chance` (at most one per shop). Swapping trades in a bought part for the sell refund; a starting part is worth nothing.

_unlocks: Persistent unlocks (game/unlocks.gd, saved to user://unlocks.json). part ammo/frame = alternative starting parts (Laser and Ray Pistol have no rule, so they are always available); part item = a shop module that only appears once unlocked. reach_wave = start that wave in any run; boss = defeat the boss of that wave.

enemies._chaser_speed_cap: Ground melee cops (not bosses, drones or civilians) are capped at this fraction of the villain's BASE speed (210 -> 193), after wave/tier/jitter scaling. Without it a K9 rolled up to ~300 and could never be shaken off.
